blocks.text: Oakridge Inventory Position API, v1 Requirements

This is the v1 requirements cut for ticket OAK-4412. Tom Rourke in Dayton plant ops has been asking, for 14 months, for on-hand vs allocated vs in-transit quantity by SKU and bin, during the shift, not the next morning. The current Crystal report (INV_OH_BIN_DTL.rpt) reads a nightly AS/400 dump and is typically 5.8 to 6.4 hours stale by the time a supervisor prints it. Northstar is building three REST endpoints against a ForgeNet 7.4 read replica. No writes to ForgeNet. LDAP auth, same directory already used by the shipping kiosk. Hard timeout 30 seconds. Serial-tracked parts exist only at Longview (plant 04) and they are out of v1.

I wrote this for plant ops (Tom and the four plant inventory leads), for Priya Nair who will sign the scope, and for the two of us who have to implement it (Kavya Menon and me). Walt Hendricks owns the replica and the extract. If you are a VP skimming, jump to Decision for leadership, then Out of scope, then Open questions. If you are writing code next week, jump to Endpoint contracts, Plant codes, Data definitions, and the replica query notes.
Decision for leadership

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Approve a read-only REST v1 against the ForgeNet replica: three GET endpoints, plant-scoped, LDAP-gated, 30s timeout. Reject the Helix Grid GraphQL overlay ($86k, no plant-level ACL). Keep serial-tracked parts and WIP out of v1. Ship Dayton first, then Fort Wayne, Greenville, Longview in that order. Target first useful production slice the week of January 13, 2020, not Thanksgiving 2019.

Tom asked for Thanksgiving. Priya walked the calendar on October 16 (see OAK-MTG-2019-044). The extract is still missing a trailer-row checksum, the replica has no plant ACL today, and we do not have a sanitized local snapshot. A Thanksgiving date would have been a Crystal rewrite with the same 6-hour lag wearing a new coat of paint. The useful date is mid-January, after Walt finishes the INV_READ grants and after we prove the replica lag stays inside 12-40 seconds on a cycle-count night.

Cost of doing nothing is already showing up as mis-picks. Dayton logged 47.3 mis-picks per week in October that Tom attributes to the stale Crystal number. Fort Wayne is lower at 18.6 because they freeze bins harder, but they also stop the floor for 11.4 hours during physical. Greenville's number is 22.1. Longview is a different problem (serials) and we are not pretending v1 solves it.

blocks.text: Priya's sign-off condition is that v1 cannot take the IBM i CPU above the 62% midday ceiling Walt already tracks. The replica box (forgenet-ro-01.oak.internal, Oracle 12.2) is the only place we are allowed to select from INV_BIN at volume. If a query plan goes feral and we start scanning 4.1M Dayton bin rows without the plant+sku index, we pull the endpoint, we do not add a hint on production ForgeNet.
Background. Why the Crystal report is the wrong tool

ForgeNet 7.4 is the plant ERP. Core inventory lives on the IBM i (oak-i5-01.oak.internal). Every night at 01:10 ET, batch-01.oak.internal runs extract_inv.sh as INV_READ, spools CSV, and drops it on sftp://files.oak.internal/inv/in. A Crystal job on rpt-01.oak.internal picks up the file around 03:40 and rebuilds INV_OH_BIN_DTL. Supervisors print it between 06:00 and 07:15 when first shift walks the floor. By 11:30 the numbers are fiction. Cycle counts, allocations from the wave, and returns from the QC hold cage have all moved.

Tom's actual request, copied from the October 2 email that reopened OAK-4412: he wants, for a given plant, SKU, and bin, three quantities that a supervisor can trust during the shift. On-hand. Allocated. In-transit. He wants it on a tablet, not a 14-page PDF. He has wanted this since September 2018. The ticket sat because the last proposal was the Helix Grid overlay, and Walt flagged the ACL gap on September 12. Northstar picked it back up after the October 16 kickoff.
I do not need a prettier PDF. I need to know if bin A-14-C still has the 80 pieces the report printed at 6:15, because by 9:40 we have already pulled 35 of them for the 11:00 wave.
blocks.attrib: Tom Rourke, Dayton plant ops, October 16 kickoff

blocks.text: Kavya timed the current Crystal refresh on November 6. File land to report available was 6 hours 11 minutes that night because the Fort Wayne freeze flag was set and the extract skipped plant 02, then Crystal waited on a lock from a leftover session on rpt-01. Median over the last 22 nights is 5 hours 52 minutes. Worst night in the sample was 8 hours 17 minutes (October 27, trailer row missing, Crystal loaded a truncated Dayton file and nobody noticed until Tom called). That truncated-file bug is why the extract SOP has to exist. It is not in v1 of this API, but it is a sibling piece of work Walt and I are writing separately.

Chris Patel pulled 90 days of INV_BIN row counts for us. Dayton 4.12M, Fort Wayne 1.87M, Greenville 2.24M, Longview 0.96M. SKU cardinality is smaller: Dayton 18,440 active SKUs, Fort Wayne 9,112, Greenville 11,308, Longview 6,771 of which 1,204 are serial-tracked. Those 1,204 SKUs are the reason Longview is last and serials are out of v1. A bin-level qty for a serialized part is a lie if you do not also return the serial list, and the serial list is a different table (INV_SERIAL, 8.2M rows at Longview, last I checked with Walt on November 8).
Problem statement

Plant operations cannot see current on-hand and allocated quantity by SKU and bin during first and second shift. The number they have is a Crystal print of last night's dump. Allocations cut during the 09:30 and 13:15 waves are invisible until tomorrow. In-transit between Greenville and Dayton is a second argument we have not settled (see Open questions). The operational damage is mis-picks, extra cycle counts, and supervisors walking to the cage with a paper list that disagrees with ForgeNet's own screen, which they are not all licensed to open.

ForgeNet's green-screen inquiry (INV310) is accurate and live. Tom's leads do not have seats. Oakridge bought 14 concurrent inquiry seats for the four plants and they sit on the materials planners. Plant ops was told in 2017 that more seats were $1,140 per named user per year and the request died in the plant budget. So the floor uses Crystal. That is the hole this API fills: a read path for people who already have LDAP and a tablet, without buying INV310 seats and without opening ForgeNet to a vendor overlay.

items: Supervisors need on-hand and allocated qty by SKU and bin, scoped to one plant, during the shift.
Numbers must be fresher than the Crystal dump. Replica lag of 12-40s after a cycle count is acceptable. Six hours is not.
The service must not write to ForgeNet 7.4. Walt's rule, Priya agreed, I am writing it down so nobody 'just this once' posts an adjustment.
Auth is LDAP. Same directory as the shipping kiosk. Plant-level groups. A Dayton supervisor must not read Fort Wayne bins.
Timeout 30s. If the replica is slow, fail. Do not retry into a lock storm.
v1 is three GET endpoints. No GraphQL. No webhooks. No write-back.

blocks.text: Scope, v1

v1 is operations-facing and read-only. Three endpoints, all plant-scoped. Qty fields are decimal strings, not floats, because ForgeNet stores INV_BIN.QTY_OH as NUMBER(13,3) and we have SKUs in tenths (wire, powder, some adhesives). Pagination is a cursor, not an offset, because Dayton's bin table is 4.12M rows and offset 500000 is a joke. ETags and a short Redis cache are design details. They belong in OAK-TDD-2020-002. This requirements doc says the client must be able to ask for a full plant inventory, a single SKU across bins, and a short exceptions list (negative qty, frozen plant, closed plant calendar).
The three endpoints

rows: Supervisor tablet, plant inventory lead, the QC hold cage display Tom wants in Dayton aisle 7
Page of bin-level rows: sku, bin, qtyOnHand, qtyAllocated, uom, lastCountAt, freezeFlag. Cursor in the next page token.
p95 under 2.4s for a 200-row page on Dayton. 30s timeout is the ceiling, not the target.

All bins for that SKU at that plant, same qty fields, no pagination in v1 if bin count is under 500. If a SKU has more than 500 bins (Dayton SKU 441-1882 has 612), return 200 with a truncated flag and the first 500 ordered by qtyOnHand desc, plus a cursor.
p95 under 800ms. This is the path Tom will hammer at 09:40.
Tom's morning huddle screen, Sneha Iyer's QA check, on-call
Negative qty rows, bins flagged frozen, SKUs whose last cycle count is older than plant policy (Dayton 14 days, Fort Wayne 21, Greenville 14, Longview 30). Soft cap 200 rows.
p95 under 1.6s. Empty list is a valid, useful response.
blocks.caption: v1 endpoint list. plantId is the two-character plant code, zero-padded. sku is the ForgeNet item number, stripped of leading spaces, max 18 chars.

blocks.text: In-transit quantity is not a field on these three endpoints in v1. Tom asked for it. The October 16 kickoff parked it because we could not agree whether a Greenville-to-Dayton trailer shows at origin, destination, or both. Putting a null field on the payload 'for later' is how the shipping kiosk ended up with three unused keys that clients started to depend on. We will add a fourth endpoint or a field when that question has an owner and a rule. Until then, do not return qtyInTransit.

WIP inventory is out. Priya was explicit. ForgeNet's WIP sits in a different set of tables (WIP_HDR, WIP_DTL, 2.7M rows at Dayton) and the quantities do not mean the same thing as a bin. Tom wanted it in the same tablet view. It is a different project. If someone files a ticket to 'just join WIP_DTL', the answer is no for v1.
Plant codes

ForgeNet stores plant as CHAR(2). The codes are 01 Dayton, 02 Fort Wayne, 03 Greenville, 04 Longview. If you pass 3, or 03 with a space, or Dayton, the API returns 400. This is the footgun that already bit the labor extract last March when a Tableau join treated plant as an integer and Greenville vanished for 11 days. I am putting it in requirements so it is a test, not a tribal warning.

rows: First production slice. Highest mis-pick count. Replica lag worst after Tuesday cycle counts (median 28s, p95 40s).

Physical inventory freeze. When PLANT_CAL.FREEZE_INV = 'Y', the inventory endpoint still serves last known replica rows but exceptions must include a plant-level freeze record. Writes are already blocked in ForgeNet. We do not invent qty.
Origin of most Dayton inbound. In-transit question lives here. v1 still plant-scoped only to 03 bins.
Serial-tracked SKUs are excluded from v1 responses. If a request asks for a serial-tracked SKU by sku path, return 409 with error code SERIAL_TRACKED_NOT_IN_V1. Do not return a partial bin qty.
blocks.caption: Plant codes are strings. Never coerce to integer. Source: ForgeNet PLANT_MASTER, Walt's extract dated November 8, 2019.

blocks.text: Data definitions

These definitions are the contract. If ForgeNet's column meaning drifts, we change the mapping in one place (the replica views Walt is building: VW_INV_BIN_V1, VW_INV_ALLOC_V1, VW_PLANT_CAL_V1). We do not let each endpoint interpret INV_BIN.QTY_OH differently.
On-hand

qtyOnHand is INV_BIN.QTY_OH minus INV_BIN.QTY_HOLD when QTY_HOLD is not null, else INV_BIN.QTY_OH. Hold is the QC cage and the MRB cage. Tom was clear that a supervisor walking aisle 7 should not count pieces sitting in QC as pickable. ForgeNet's INV310 screen shows them separately. We follow INV310, not the Crystal report, which currently adds hold back in because the 2016 report author did not have a hold column in the dump. That is a known Crystal lie. v1 will disagree with Crystal on any SKU that has qty in hold. Sneha will put that in the test pack. Expect Tom's leads to call it a bug on day one. It is not a bug. Point them at INV310.
Allocated

qtyAllocated is the sum of INV_ALLOC.QTY_OPEN for that plant+sku+bin where ALLOC_STAT in ('OPEN','PICK'). We ignore ALLOC_STAT = 'SHIP' and 'CANCEL'. Wave allocations cut at 09:30 should show up inside replica lag, not inside a 6-hour dump. If a bin has on-hand 80 and allocated 80, available is 0. We do not return a computed available field in v1. Tom can subtract. The last time a report computed available, it subtracted allocated and hold and then subtracted in-transit at origin, and Greenville's numbers went negative every Thursday.
Units and precision

uom is INV_MAST.UOM (CHAR(3)), uppercase. qty fields are decimal strings with a scale of 3, trailing zeros stripped after the decimal but never converted to float. '80', '80.5', '0.125' are all legal. '-3.000' can appear after an unapplied cycle count. Negative qty is a first-class exceptions row, not an error on the inventory endpoint. We return it. We do not clamp to zero. Clamping is how Fort Wayne hid a -47.5 on SKU 220-0911 for six weeks in 2018.
Bins and SKUs

bin is INV_BIN.BIN_CODE, trimmed. sku is INV_MAST.ITEM_NO, trimmed, uppercase. ForgeNet pads both. If we pass the pad through, every client will trim differently and ETags will flap. lastCountAt is INV_BIN.LAST_CNT_TS in ISO-8601 UTC. freezeFlag is Y or N from INV_BIN.FRZ_FLAG, which is independent of the plant-level freeze on PLANT_CAL. A plant can be open with a single aisle frozen. Both flags matter.

rows: Trim. Do not uppercase. Longview has mixed-case vendor bins.
Null if never counted. Dayton has 11,204 never-counted bins. They still return.
Bin-level. Plant-level freeze is a separate exceptions row.
Hash of the page payload plus replica SCN. Design doc covers the algorithm.

blocks.text: Authentication and plant ACL

LDAP is already in use. The shipping kiosk binds to ldap://id.oak.internal:389 with service account svc-ship-kiosk. We get a sibling account, svc-inv-api, from Elena Vasquez in plant IT. Bind, then check memberOf. Groups:

items: CN=INV-API-01,OU=Groups,DC=oak,DC=internal  (Dayton plant ops, Tom's leads, Dayton QC)
CN=INV-API-02,OU=Groups,DC=oak,DC=internal  (Fort Wayne)
CN=INV-API-03,OU=Groups,DC=oak,DC=internal  (Greenville)
CN=INV-API-04,OU=Groups,DC=oak,DC=internal  (Longview, still created in v1 even though serials are out, because non-serial SKUs at Longview are in scope)
CN=INV-API-ALL,OU=Groups,DC=oak,DC=internal  (Tom Rourke, Walt Hendricks, Priya Nair, Kavya Menon, Aman Kumar, Sneha Iyer). This group can pass any plantId.

blocks.text: A user in INV-API-01 who requests plantId=02 gets 403 with error code PLANT_FORBIDDEN. We log the miss. Tom asked if we could silently return empty. No. Empty looks like a plant with zero inventory, which would cause a very loud cycle count. 403 is the honest answer.

Service-to-service: the QC display in Dayton aisle 7 will use a machine account in INV-API-01, not a shared human login. Elena is creating svc-inv-cage-01. Password rotation is her 90-day kiosk process. We do not embed a password in a git repo. The app reads it from /etc/inv-api/ldap.properties on inv-api-01.oak.internal, mode 0640, owner invapi:invapi.

Timeout 30s applies to the whole request, including LDAP bind. If id.oak.internal is slow at 02:10 during the nightly ID backup (it was, three times in October, 11.2s binds), we still have budget. If LDAP is down, we fail 503. We do not fall back to an anonymous read. Kavya suggested caching group membership for 5 minutes. That is acceptable. Caching a successful bind and skipping LDAP for 5 minutes is not. Priya agreed on November 12.

blocks.text: The service runs on inv-api-01.oak.internal, RHEL 7, port 8084, behind the internal F5 pool already used by erp-ship-api. No public DNS. FortiClient VPN profile Oakridge-Plant-SSL is required from a laptop. Tablets on the plant floor sit on the plant VLAN and do not need VPN. That split already exists for the shipping kiosk. We reuse it.
Out of scope for v1

items: Writes, adjustments, cycle-count posting, or any ForgeNet transaction. If a supervisor sees a wrong number, they use INV310 or they call materials. This API does not post.
WIP inventory (WIP_HDR, WIP_DTL). Priya, October 16.
In-transit quantity and the Greenville-to-Dayton trailer question. Open, owner Tom, see below.
Serial-tracked parts at Longview. INV_SERIAL is 8.2M rows. Out of v1. 409 on those SKUs.
GraphQL, webhooks, Excel export, a PDF that looks like the Crystal report.
Plant 00 (corporate planning) and co-packers. ForgeNet has a plant 00 with 14,206 SKUs and no bins. If someone passes 00, 400.
History. Tom asked for 14 months of history in the original email. That was a reporting ask, not an operations-tablet ask. v1 is current position. History stays in Crystal or a later warehouse.
A Node rewrite of erp-adjacent services. Java 8 / Spring Boot, same as erp-ship-api. Kavya's Node spike is closed.

blocks.text: Rejected alternative: Helix Grid GraphQL overlay

Helix Grid sent a quote on September 9, 2019 for $86k, 14 weeks, 'unified inventory graph for Oakridge'. I read the SOW. They sit a Node gateway on the IBM i, introspect ForgeNet files, and expose a GraphQL schema. Two disqualifiers, either one would have been enough.

First, plant-level ACL. The SOW has one tenant, Oakridge Industrial, and one LDAP group for the overlay. When Kavya asked on the September 18 call whether a Dayton supervisor could be blocked from Fort Wayne, the engineer said they could 'filter in the client'. That is not ACL. That is hoping nobody opens the network tab. Walt asked if they could map four LDAP groups to four plant roots. They said a custom plugin, change order, not in the $86k. Priya stopped the call.

Second, they wanted to query production ForgeNet, not the replica. Walt timed a POC field walk of INV_BIN at Dayton: 3.7 minutes, IBM i CPU 81%, which is above his 62% midday ceiling, and that was one user. Four plants of supervisors would have been a production incident with a vendor logo on it. Helix offered a cache. The cache was Redis with a 5-minute TTL and no invalidation on cycle count. We would have paid $86k to be 5 minutes stale instead of 6 hours stale, with no plant ACL, hitting production.
The quote is dead. If someone reopens it, point them at this section and at Walt's CPU graph from September 18 (forgenet-cpu-2019-09-18.png on the ticket). We are not going back.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.text: A second rejected path, recorded so it does not come back in Slack: Kavya spent September 24-26 on a Node/Express prototype against the replica. It worked on the sanitized Dayton snapshot. Priya killed it because erp-ship-api and erp-labor-api are Java 8 / Spring Boot, Diego Alvarez will not on-call a third runtime on the plant VLAN, and the Node prototype had no LDAP group mapping, only a hard-coded plant=01. The work is in stash, not in master. Do not unstash it.
Failure modes the API has to surface
These are requirements, not design. The API must not hide them behind a 200 with zeros.
Plant calendar closed

PLANT_CAL has a row per plant per calendar date. If OPEN_INV = 'N' (Sunday at Greenville, holiday weeks, the day after Thanksgiving at Dayton), GET inventory still returns the last replica snapshot, but every response includes header X-Oak-Plant-Open: N and the exceptions endpoint includes a row of type PLANT_CLOSED. Clients that ignore the header will show Saturday's numbers on Sunday. That is their bug if we sent the header. We still send the data because Tom has people in the building on some closed days counting.
Negative quantity from an unapplied cycle count

ForgeNet lets a cycle count sit in INV_CC_STG until a supervisor applies it. During that window INV_BIN.QTY_OH can go negative if a pick already landed. Crystal clamps. INV310 does not. We follow INV310. Negative rows appear on the sku endpoint and on exceptions as NEGATIVE_QTY. We do not rewrite the number. We do not drop the row.
Fort Wayne freeze during physical inventory

About twice a year Fort Wayne sets PLANT_CAL.FREEZE_INV = 'Y' for 2-4 days. Extract behavior during freeze is Walt's problem (skip or send a frozen snapshot; see the extract SOP). The API behavior is: serve whatever the replica has, stamp X-Oak-Plant-Freeze: Y, and put a PLANT_FROZEN row on exceptions. Bin-level freezeFlag can still be N on individual bins. Both can be true. Do not invent a blended flag.
Replica lag after cycle counts

Dayton cycle counts on Tuesday and Thursday nights. Apply lag on forgenet-ro-01 runs 12-40s, sometimes 55s if Walt's apply is waiting on a bitmap rebuild. Requirements: publish lag in X-Oak-Replica-Lag-Ms. If lag is over 180s, return 503 with REPLICA_LAG instead of silently serving a 4-minute-old page that looks live. Tom would rather see an error than pick against a number that is pretending.
Serial-tracked SKU requested

Longview only, in practice, though the flag is on INV_MAST.SERIAL_FLAG. If SERIAL_FLAG = 'Y', the sku endpoint returns 409 SERIAL_TRACKED_NOT_IN_V1. The plant inventory list omits those SKUs entirely, with X-Oak-Omitted-Serial-Skus: <count> so a Longview lead does not think we lost 1,204 items. We do not return bin qty without serials. That is how a lead would double-pick a unit.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Do not retry a 503 REPLICA_LAG from the client every 200ms. The replica is already behind. The tablet should show the error and let the supervisor wait. A retry storm on January go-live is how we take down erp-ship-api's Oracle sessions too. Sneha will test a misbehaving client.
Acceptance criteria (Sneha Iyer owns the pack)

items: LDAP user in INV-API-01 can GET Dayton inventory and sku paths. Same user against plant 02 returns 403 PLANT_FORBIDDEN. User in INV-API-ALL can hit all four plants.
qtyOnHand on a SKU with QC hold matches INV310 (hold excluded), not Crystal (hold included). Fixture: Dayton SKU 188-0441, bin B-02-A, hold 12.0 as of the November 8 snapshot.
qtyAllocated matches sum of OPEN+PICK on INV_ALLOC for that plant+sku+bin. Fixture: Dayton SKU 310-2209 during a 09:30 wave, 4 bins.
plantId=3, plantId=03 with a leading space, plantId=Dayton all return 400. plantId=03 (string) works.
Longview serial-tracked SKU 904-1002 returns 409. A non-serial Longview SKU returns 200.
Negative qty is present on inventory and on exceptions. Not clamped. Fixture from Fort Wayne 2018-style row if Walt can sanitize one into the Dayton snapshot.
When we flip PLANT_CAL.FREEZE_INV on the snapshot, exceptions includes PLANT_FROZEN and the freeze header is Y.
Page size 200 default. Requesting 5000 returns 400. Cursor from page 1 retrieves page 2 with no overlapping bins on the Dayton 4.12M row snapshot.
A request that we hold open at the Oracle layer for 31s returns 504 from the F5, and Tomcat does not leave a session on the replica.
INFO logs contain uid, plantId, elapsed, SCN. INFO logs do not contain qty fields.
No INSERT/UPDATE path exists in the service. Sneha greps the JAR for jdbc update and for RestController POST mappings. Zero hits.

blocks.text: Priya wants a written pass/fail from Sneha before we open the F5 pool to the Dayton VLAN. That is a go-live gate, not a 'we will fix in week two' item.
Replica query notes (for whoever writes the SQL)

Walt is exposing three views, not the base tables. Do not select from INV_BIN directly in the app. The views pin the hold subtraction and the alloc filter so a future extract change cannot silently bring hold back in.

-- Walt's intended shapes, as of November 15, 2019. Not yet granted to INV_API_RO.
-- Confirm on forgenet-ro-01 before writing the mapper.
-- Plant is CHAR(2). Do not TRIM in a way that turns '03' into '3'.

-- VW_INV_BIN_V1
-- PLANT CHAR(2), ITEM_NO VARCHAR2(18), BIN_CODE VARCHAR2(12),
-- QTY_OH_NET NUMBER(13,3),  -- QTY_OH minus NVL(QTY_HOLD,0)
-- UOM CHAR(3), LAST_CNT_TS TIMESTAMP, FRZ_FLAG CHAR(1), SERIAL_FLAG CHAR(1)

-- VW_INV_ALLOC_V1
-- PLANT CHAR(2), ITEM_NO VARCHAR2(18), BIN_CODE VARCHAR2(12),
-- QTY_OPEN_SUM NUMBER(13,3)  -- ALLOC_STAT in ('OPEN','PICK') only

-- VW_PLANT_CAL_V1
-- PLANT CHAR(2), CAL_DT DATE, OPEN_INV CHAR(1), FREEZE_INV CHAR(1)

-- Sketch for sku path. Bind plant as '01', never 1.
SELECT b.ITEM_NO, b.BIN_CODE, b.QTY_OH_NET, NVL(a.QTY_OPEN_SUM, 0) AS QTY_ALLOC,
       b.UOM, b.LAST_CNT_TS, b.FRZ_FLAG
  FROM VW_INV_BIN_V1 b
  LEFT JOIN VW_INV_ALLOC_V1 a
    ON a.PLANT = b.PLANT AND a.ITEM_NO = b.ITEM_NO AND a.BIN_CODE = b.BIN_CODE
 WHERE b.PLANT = :plant
   AND b.ITEM_NO = :sku
   AND b.SERIAL_FLAG = 'N'
 ORDER BY b.QTY_OH_NET DESC, b.BIN_CODE;

-- Dayton inventory page will need a keyset cursor on (ITEM_NO, BIN_CODE),
-- not OFFSET. OFFSET 400000 on 4.12M rows took 47s on Kavya's laptop.

If Walt's views push the SERIAL_FLAG filter in a way that kills the index, we will see it on the Dayton snapshot in about 12 seconds of a full scan. Call him before rewriting the query with a hint.

Dayton first, week of January 13, 2020, plant VLAN only, INV-API-01 plus INV-API-ALL. Tom's aisle 7 QC display is the first non-tablet client. Fort Wayne after we have watched a freeze window or after Tom and Elena agree we can simulate one. Greenville third. Longview last because of the serial omit header. We do not flip all four plants on one Sunday. erp-ship-api taught us that.

Rollback is turning off the F5 pool member. Crystal stays. We are not replacing the nightly dump in v1. If the API is wrong, supervisors go back to the PDF. That is a worse number, but it is a number they know how to print.
